checks.label: In a simple truss, m = 2j − 3, where m is the total number of members and j is the number of joints: every frame here grown one triangle at a time (the triangles, the braced square, the braced square with its roof, the two braced bays, the frame of five triangles) has exactly 2j − 3 bars and no way left to move
A triangular truss of three members connected at three joints is clearly a rigid truss: the triangle has no way to move, while a drag on the square's top corner folds it, every bar keeping its length

If an object is balanced, the total clockwise moment about a pivot is equal to the total anticlockwise moment about that pivot: the supports' pushes, found by balancing every joint, balance the load's moment about either support (10 kN at mid-span gives 5 kN each; 12 kN 2 m from the left of a 6 m span gives 8 kN and 4 kN)

If the force exerted by a member on a pin is directed toward that pin, the member is in compression; if it is directed away from the pin, the member is in tension: every bar arrow drawn at a pin points away from it exactly when its bar pulls, and each bar's label says pull or push to match
Every joint is in balance: at each joint of each loaded frame the bar forces, the load and the support pushes add to nothing, so each nose-to-tail drawing closes back on its start

The figures come from the rule: 2 × 3 − 3 = 3, 2 × 4 − 3 = 5 and 2 × 6 − 3 = 9; 10 kN at the top joint gives 5 kN pushes, 10 kN in each 30° bar and 8.66 kN in the bottom bar; 12 kN at 45° gives 8.49 kN and 6.00 kN; 12 kN at 2 m of 6 m gives 8 kN and 4 kN; π × 20 = 62.8 mm, 62.8 ÷ 2 = 31.4 and 62.8 ÷ 1.5 = 41.9; 2 × 5 − 3 = 7

Each typed answer and slip is worked from the lesson's figures: 7 bars (6, 10, 5), 1 bar (4, 9, 0), 8 kN (4, 6), 8.66 kN (10, 5, 11.55), 41.9 times (31.4, 13.3, 94.2) and 8.49 kN (6, 12, 4.24); each answer as printed is graded right and each slip wrong

Every pose a frame can be dragged into keeps each bar's length and each foot on its support: the square without a diagonal, with or without its roof, and the two bays with one bay unbraced, each have exactly one way left to move, and that is the motion drawn
Before an answer nothing gives it away: each asked figure reads "?", no bar is labelled pull or push, and the frames stand unmoved; after it, each shows

The mechanical advantage of a screw can be found by dividing the circumference of the screw by the pitch (lead) of the screw: one turn of each screw drawn unrolls into a ramp as long as its circumference that climbs one pitch, and its load lifted ÷ push is that length ÷ the pitch, more for the finer thread
The choices follow the rule: the triangle holds and the square folds; with a load at its top joint only the triangle's bottom bar pulls; of the two frames with 9 bars only Frame B can move
Every demonstration settles within 5 s of its screen opening, and every answer's motion within 3.5 s
